verdict.rationale: Homebrew documents that it installs each package into its own keg inside a single global Cellar and symlinks it into the prefix. Combined with project Brewfiles that install into that same system-wide prefix, this implies one stored copy per installed version shared by every project. Nothing shows the store is content-addressable (hash-keyed), and per-project deduplication is only implied by the global install model. Missing for 10: any evidence of content-addressable (hash-based) storage, explicit documentation of cross-project deduplication of identical versions, and independent or hands-on corroboration of disk savings.
